page.overview:
Who is Beltran?

Beltran, also called Beltran the Perspicacious, was a Wizard Lord of the Celestial College, a contemporary and rival to the Jade Wizard Garvan Paranoth, the supreme patriarch of the Imperial Colleges of Magic in 2383 IC. Where Paranoth argued the importance of raw experience in understanding magic, Beltran claimed introspection and contemplation provided true insight -- and that mundane life merely confused the mind. This may explain why Beltran was so unpopular amongst his peers and preferred to live away from the Celestial College in an isolated tower outside Eilhart.

Paranoth and Beltran's disagreements escalated into attacks on one another's reputation and eventually violence. Duels between magisters were common at the time, so it was not unusual for differing opinions to turn into open battles. The Jade Wizard was an inventive spellcaster, but Beltran was an accomplished prognosticator, able to foresee Paranoth's attacks and prepare an appropriate counter-spell. The stalemate was broken when Beltran's political unpopularity in the Celestial College proved his undoing -- Wizard Lord Otto von Heiermat quietly told Paranoth of several blind spots in Beltran's foresight.

The monument outside Eilhart, known as Paranoth's Column, is the result of Paranoth's final victory. After walking on foot from Altdorf to Eilhart, the Jade Wizard cast Paranoth's Hastened Sprouting for the first and last time. Beltran was caught in his tower as vegetation tore into the stonework, erupted through the floors, and engulfed the whole structure. The astromancer was killed and the academic dispute resolved, so Paranoth left for the Far East. Otto von Heiermat covered up Beltran's fate -- he is now but a half-forgotten footnote in the Celestial College's history.

Within Paranoth's Column there exists a pool filled with rainwater. By descending into the depths, which are actually the drowned remains of Beltran's tower, including his preserved grimoires, one will discover a weed-covered orrery outfitted with a model of Morrslieb created from real warpstone, and the astromancer's skeleton, pierced by the sharp branches that took his life.
